/-!
# Conjecture 10.40

by G. A. Noskov

(H. Bass). Let $G$ be a group, $e$ an idempotent matrix over $\mathbb{Z}G$ and let
$\operatorname{tr} e = \sum_{g \in G} e_g g$, $e_g \in \mathbb{Z}$.

*Strong conjecture:* for any non-trivial $x \in G$, the equation $\sum_{g \sim x} e_g = 0$
holds, where $\sim$ denotes conjugacy in $G$.

*Weak conjecture:* $\sum_{g \in G} e_g = 0$.

The strong conjecture has been proved for finite, abelian and linear groups and the weak
conjecture has been proved for residually finite groups.

H. Bass' Comment of 2005: Significant progress has been made; a good up-to-date account is in
the paper (A. J. Berrick, I. Chatterji, G. Mislin, *Math. Ann.* **329** (2004), 597–621).

These are Bass' integral trace conjectures. The function $x \mapsto \sum_{g \sim x} e_g$ on
conjugacy classes is the Hattori–Stallings rank of the finitely generated projective
$\mathbb{Z}G$-module defined by $e$.

The formula printed for the weak conjecture is a misprint: $\sum_{g \in G} e_g$ is the
augmentation of $\operatorname{tr} e$, which equals $1$ for the $1 \times 1$ identity matrix.
Bass' weak conjecture states $\sum_{g \in G} e_g = e_1$, i.e. $\sum_{g \ne 1} e_g = 0$; this
is what the strong conjecture gives after summing over all non-trivial conjugacy classes, and
it is the form stated below.

The integral group ring $\mathbb{Z}G$ is `MonoidAlgebra ℤ G`, and the coefficient $e_g$ is the
value `e.trace g` of the trace `e.trace : MonoidAlgebra ℤ G` at `g`. Since the trace has finite
support, each sum is written as a finite sum over the support of the trace.

*References:*
- [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46), Problem 10.40
- H. Bass, *Euler characteristics and characters of discrete groups*, Invent. Math. 35 (1976),
  155–196
- A. J. Berrick, I. Chatterji, G. Mislin, *From acyclic groups to the Bass conjecture for
  amenable groups*, [Math. Ann. 329 (2004), 597–621](https://doi.org/10.1007/s00208-004-0521-6)
-/

blocks.docstring:
**Bass' strong conjecture.** Let $G$ be a group, $e$ an idempotent $n \times n$ matrix over
the integral group ring $\mathbb{Z}G$, and write $\operatorname{tr} e = \sum_{g \in G} e_g g$
with $e_g \in \mathbb{Z}$. Then for every non-trivial $x \in G$,
$$\sum_{g \sim x} e_g = 0,$$
where $\sim$ denotes conjugacy in $G$.

Here `e.trace g` is the coefficient $e_g$. Only finitely many $e_g$ are non-zero, so the sum
over the conjugacy class of $x$ is taken over the elements of the support of
$\operatorname{tr} e$ that are conjugate to $x$.

blocks.docstring:
**Bass' weak conjecture.** Let $G$ be a group, $e$ an idempotent $n \times n$ matrix over
the integral group ring $\mathbb{Z}G$, and write $\operatorname{tr} e = \sum_{g \in G} e_g g$
with $e_g \in \mathbb{Z}$. Then
$$\sum_{g \in G,\ g \ne 1} e_g = 0,$$
equivalently $\sum_{g \in G} e_g = e_1$.

The notebook prints $\sum_{g \in G} e_g = 0$, which is a misprint: it fails for the
$1 \times 1$ identity matrix. The statement above is Bass' weak conjecture, the consequence of
the strong conjecture obtained by summing over all non-trivial conjugacy classes.

claims.decomposer_note: Universally quantified over every group G, every n and every idempotent n×n matrix e over the integral group ring ℤG (MonoidAlgebra ℤ G); e_g is the coefficient of g in the trace tr e = Σ_i e_ii, which has finite support so the sum over the conjugacy class {g : IsConj x g} is finite; this is Bass's strong trace conjecture (Hattori–Stallings rank vanishes off the identity), still open in general (the special cases finite/abelian/linear/amenable groups mentioned in the statement and in Berrick–Chatterji–Mislin 2004 are proven results, not questions).
claims.reviewer_why: All eight candidates state the same proposition: for every group G, n, idempotent e : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) (MonoidAlgebra ℤ G) and x ≠ 1, the sum of the coefficients e.trace g over {g | IsConj x g} is 0. I verified in Lean that e.trace g is definitionally the coefficient of g in Σ_i e_ii, that IsConj is ordinary group conjugacy, and that the finsum versions (c03/c08) are provably equal to the filtered-support Finset sums (c01/c02/c04-c07), so every candidate is faithful. c02 chosen for style: Type* with explicit hypotheses (matching Wikipedia/Kaplansky.lean), transparent Finset filter over the finite support (no reliance on finsum's infinite-support default), full source text and misprint discussion in docstrings. Boundary cases: trivial G is vacuous (no x ≠ 1), n = 0 gives zero trace; neither alters the claim.
claims.source_text: Strong conjecture: for any non-trivial $x \in G$, the equation $\sum\limits_{g\sim x} e_g=0$ holds where $\sim $ denotes conjugacy in $G$.
claims.text_span:
{\it Strong
conjecture:\/} for any non-trivial $x \in G$, the equation
$\sum\limits_{g\sim x} e_g=0$ holds where $\sim $ denotes
conjugacy in $G$.

claims.decomposer_note: The literal formula Σ_{g∈G} e_g = 0 is a misprint (false for the 1×1 identity matrix, whose trace is 1); Bass's weak conjecture is Σ_{g≠1} e_g = 0, i.e. the augmentation ε(tr e) = Σ_g e_g equals the identity coefficient e_1, which is exactly the consequence of the strong conjecture obtained by summing over all non-trivial conjugacy classes, hence a subordinate weaker form (open in general; proven for residually finite groups per the statement).
claims.reviewer_why: All candidates follow the decomposition table's corrected reading Σ_{g≠1} e_g = 0 (equivalently augmentation of tr e equals e_1). I confirmed in Lean that the literal notebook formula Σ_{g∈G} e_g = 0 evaluates to 1 for the 1×1 identity matrix (so it is a misprint), while the corrected form gives 0 there; the corrected form is exactly the consequence of the strong conjecture summed over all non-trivial conjugacy classes and is Bass' weak conjecture as stated in Bass (1976). c02's `∑ g ∈ e.trace.support with g ≠ 1, e.trace g = 0` is equivalent to c05's `.erase 1`, c04/c06's `.filter`, and c03/c08's finsum forms. c02 chosen for consistency with the strong slot and for docstrings that record the misprint.

decomposition_objections.text: None. I agree the weak-conjecture formula as printed is a misprint and that Σ_{g≠1} e_g = 0 (equivalently Σ_g e_g = e_1) is Bass' weak conjecture; I followed the table's reading.

items: Both slots are stated as direct theorems (not `answer(sorry) ↔ …`) because the source states conjectures, not yes/no questions; the group G, size n, matrix e, and the element x are theorem arguments rather than bound inside a ∀.
Matrices are indexed by `Fin n` (n × n square matrices); any finite index type would be equivalent.
Idempotency is `IsIdempotentElem e` (e * e = e) in the matrix ring over `MonoidAlgebra ℤ G`.

The sum over the conjugacy class of x is written as the finite sum over `e.trace.support` filtered by `IsConj x g` (classical decidability via `open scoped Classical in`), which equals Σ_{g∼x} e_g since coefficients off the support are 0.

Weak conjecture: the literal notebook formula Σ_{g∈G} e_g = 0 is a misprint (false for the 1×1 identity matrix); following the decomposition table and Bass' original weak conjecture (ε(tr e) = e_1), it is stated as Σ_{g≠1} e_g = 0, i.e. `∑ g ∈ e.trace.support with g ≠ 1, e.trace g = 0`. The equivalent form Σ_g e_g = e_1 is mentioned in the docstring.

Both statements are tagged `research open` (the strong and weak Bass conjectures are open for general groups); the proven special cases (finite, abelian, linear, residually finite, amenable groups) mentioned in the statement are not stated as separate declarations since they are not part of the decomposition table.
AMS tags 16 (associative rings/group rings), 19 (K-theory/projective modules), 20 (group theory).

reviewer_notes: The only interpretive issue is the weak conjecture's printed formula Σ_{g∈G} e_g = 0, which is false as printed (1×1 identity matrix has trace 1 ∈ ℤG; checked in Lean). The final file states Bass' actual weak conjecture Σ_{g≠1} e_g = 0 (ε(tr e) = e_1), as directed by the decomposition table and as agreed by every candidate; both docstrings document the correction. No candidate omitted a slot, and no omission reasons needed weighing. The eight candidates are mathematically identical (finsum vs Finset-filter encodings proven equal in a scratch file); the final file is c02 with light docstring edits. Compiles with `lake env lean --json` reporting only the two `declaration uses 'sorry'` warnings. Proven special cases (finite/abelian/linear/residually finite/amenable groups) are not slots and are not stated.
